title: Microscopy & Biological Scales
description: Microscope calibration, biological scale, and observations of the termite gut community

blocks.text:
Write a brief summary of the Introduction to Microscopy experiment, and what we
sought to learn. You summary should be between one paragraph and one page in
length.

The Introduction to Microscopy experiment is to gain an understanding of biological scales, observing through a microscope the active and complex ecosystems down to as small and mundane as a termite gut. Using brightfield imagine equipped with 10x, 40x and 100x lenses, we explored the ecosystem within a worker termite gut, observing protozoa and microbes that allow a termite to digest wood(lignocellulose). We captured images taken on each lens, focusing on finding examples of protozoa such as Trichonympha, Streblomastix and Trichomitopsis. We successfully found these such examples, and took notes of different organisms we found while looking through the microscope, clear images were taken on the 10x and 40x lenses but due to the longer exposure time and the speed some of these organisms were travelling at, the images on the 100x lens were quite blurry, making it difficult to analyze the target organism.

When is it ok to look into the microscope eye pieces? When is it not ok?

As the brightfield illumination can be incredibly strong, only look through the eye piece after preparing sample, condenser and objective, and that the fluorescence beam is off and the light source is set to the lowest setting. Then look through the eye piece and slowly increase the strength of the light source until it is at a suitable strength.

In this course, we will work with several model organisms. We will work with E.
coli, S. cerevisiae, C. elegans, and the termite Zootermopsis nevadensis. (In the past,
we have also worked with Drosophila melanogaster) Of course, we also have Homo
sapiens running around lab. Approximately how big are each of these organisms?
The excellent BioNumbers website is a great resource for these numbers and many
many others.

- E.Coli - 1-2µmin length and 0.5µm in diameter
- S. cerevisiae - ovoid cell 7.5x5.5µm
- C. Elegans - 1mm in length and 80µm in diameter
- Zootermopsis nevadensis - 10-12mm in length, alates(reproductive individuals) up to 1.9cm
- Drosophila melanogaster - 3mm in length
- Homosapiens - This one - 1.69m in length , average height of 1.6-1.75m

Use your images of the graticule to determine the interpixel spacing at 10×, 40×,
and 100× magnification. You will need to use some of the image processing skills
you learned in the tutorials. Remember to turn in your code for full credit.

- 10x : 0.58µm
- 40x : 0.15µm
- 100x : 0.058µm

blocks.text:
Much can be learned about life simply by watching and making some estimates. Using the observations you made of the termite gut, make the following estimates. For each estimate, be sure to explain your thought process and show any and all approximations you made. For this problem, do not use any resources other than your brain, your experiences in this lab, a paper, and pen (no calculators or internet). - **a)** What is the volume of the termite gut?
Unfortunately as Prof Bois performed the extraction of the termite gut, I don't have a precise estimate of the proportions. When he pulled out the gut, it seemed to be about a sixth of the length of the termite. Since it seemed to be a smaller one, I'll assume it's length to be 1cm, so the length of the gut is about 6mm, and from what i saw, though it was not uniform in diameter, it is somewhere between 0.5mm to 1mm, I'll estimate it as 0,75mm. Taking the cross sectional area to be pi r^2, that makes it just about 0.5mm^2, and the length as 6mm, the volume is about 3mm^3. - **b)** What is the concentration of protists and microbes within the gut? Remember that you diluted the protists when you added TGF that you diluted the protists when you added TGF.
I estimate that the volume of TGF added to be around 10x the volume of the termite gut, so I should multiply the concentration of microbes/protists seen by 10x to estimate the concentration of protists and microbes within the gut. In the 10xOB1 image, the area is 1160µm x 720µm (using interpixel distance of around 0.6µm), around 800000µm^2, which is about 0.8mm^2, and I count about 80, which makes the concentration about 100 per mm^2, and since it is diluted, the gut concentration of protists and microbes is about 1000 per mm^2, or 1000000 per mm^3. - **c)** What is the ratio of bacteria and archaea to eukaryotic protists in terms of volume and in terms of number?
Streblomastix is the main type of bacteria, while trichonympha and trichomitopsis are the main eukaryotic protists, from the 10xOB1 image again, the number ratio is about 3:5 (protists:bacteria) and in volume, 50:1 (protists:bacteria) - **d)** How many different species of Trichonympha, Streblomastix, and Trichomitopsis are in the termite gut? Think about this estimate carefully.
From the lab notebook, we have noted down different observations. For streblomastix, due to their size and lack of discerning features, I cannot tell if there was more than 1 species, for Trichonympha there seems to be 2 (one oblong and one spherical), and for trichomitopsis, there seems to be one main species.

The termite gut, as you’ve just seen, is far from boring sludge. While studied for
decades, very little is known about how the microbial and protist community works
with one another to survive. In fact, the role that many of the protists play in the
gut is entirely unknown! Based on your observations in the lab, write three topics of
the termite gut you think would be interesting to study and why. There is no right
answer to this question, so be creative!

1. How do these microbes help a termite digest wood? (To understand the biological processes of how to harness energy from such a hard to digest material)
2. Does the variety of microbes in a termite differ if they suit a different purpose in a colony (soldier, worker etc)? (Does the gut microbes change depending on how the energy generated is spent)
3. At what stage after birth do these microbes get introduced into a termite's gut? (Are these microbes essential at an early stage?, and how do microbes get into a termite in the first stage, through other termites?)

Show an image from each magnification you used to observe the termite gut protists.
Write a brief explanation of the type of organisms that are visible in the field of view.
Be sure your axes have appropriate units so that we can tell the scale of the images
we are looking at.

blocks.text: Observations: Here is an image at 10x magnification, we can see the large eukaryotic protists, with more trichonympha than trichomitopsis, the trichonympha are the pear shaped larger and wider ones, with a narrow "mouth" on one end, and the trichomitposis are smaller and longer shaped, they alsy seem to have less "stuff" inside them. We can also see small Streblomastix bacteria moving around, they are thin little strips.
